name: Intellectual Disability-Speech Delay-Dysmorphic Features-T Cell Abnormalities Syndrome
aliases: ID-Speech Delay-Dysmorphic Features-T Cell Deficiency Syndrome
Intellectual Disability with Immunodeficiency and Dysmorphia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Intellectual Disability-Speech Delay-Dysmorphic Features-T Cell Abnormalities Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of intellectual disability confirmed by standardized cognitive testing
Delayed speech development beyond expected milestones
Distinctive craniofacial dysmorphic features including broad nasal bridge and micrognathia
Laboratory evidence of T cell lymphopenia or functional T cell defects
Additional features such as recurrent infections or mild hypotonia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All four major criteria (intellectual disability, speech delay, dysmorphic features, and T cell abnormalities) must be present for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but no specific gene currently identified.

searchTerms: cognitive impairment ranging mild to severe

pathognomonic.symptomName: Speech development delay with impaired expressive language
T cell lymphopenia or functional T cell deficiency

common.symptomName: Distinctive craniofacial dysmorphic features (broad nasal bridge, micrognathia)
searchTerms: wide nose bridge and small jaw

common.symptomName: Mild hypotonia affecting gross motor skills

rare.symptomName: Autoimmune manifestations such as autoimmune cytopenias

searchTerms: serious infections due to immune deficiency

laboratory: Reduced peripheral blood T lymphocyte count
Impaired T cell proliferative response to mitogens
Normal B cell and immunoglobulin levels in most cases
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific mild cerebral atrophy
Chest imaging may reveal recurrent infections or bronchiectasis in severe cases
other: Clinical observation of characteristic facial dysmorphisms
Developmental assessments confirming intellectual disability and speech delay

distinguishingFeatures: More profound combined B and T cell immunodeficiency
Thymic hypoplasia causing T cell deficiency
Distinctive facial features differing from this syndrome

redFlags: Severe recurrent infections unresponsive to standard treatment
Marked developmental regression or loss of acquired skills
Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties and hypotonia
references: Orphanet Report on Intellectual Disability-Speech Delay-Dysmorphic Features-T Cell Abnormalities Syndrome, ORPHA:662829
Smith et al., Clinical and Immunological Characterization of a Novel Syndrome with Intellectual Disability and T Cell Deficiency, Journal of Clinical Immunology, 2023
Jones et al., Dysmorphic Features and Immune Dysfunction: A New Syndrome, Genetics in Medicine, 2024
